ja: ולבאס וכן ונכאח, פאמרהא באלתערץ' אלי אסתג'לאבהא באלאסבאב אלמהיאה להא עלי וג'וה מכ'צוצה ופי אוקאת מעלומה, פמא קדר אללה אן יתם ללאנסאן מנהא יתם וצח בצחהֵ תאתי אלאסבאב, ומא לם יקדר אללה לה תמאמה מנהא לם יתם ותעד'רת עליה אלאסבאב, וצחת מנה אלטאעה ואלמעציה ללה ג'ל ועז באלקצד ואלאכ'תיאר לאחדאהמא דון אלאכ'רי, ווג'ב ד'לך אלת'ואב ואלעקאב ואן לם יצח ללאנסאן תנפיד' אלפעל להא. ואלוג'ה אלת'אני אן אלאנסאן לו כפי אלשקא ואלתערץ' ואלתסבב פי אסתג'לאב רזקה לאשר ובטר ובאדר אלי אלמעאצי, ולם ילתפת אלי חקוק נעמהֵ אללה עליה, כקולה והיה כנור ונבל תוף וחליל ויין משתיהם ואת פועל ה' לא יביטו ומעשה ידיו לא ראו, וקאל וישמן ישורון ויבעט שמנת עבית כשית ויטש אלוה עשהו. וקאל אלאואיל יפה תלמוד תורה עם דרך ארץ שיגיעת שניהם משכחת עון, וכל תורה שאין עמה מלאכה סופה בטלה וגוררת עון. ואחרי מן חרמהמא ג'מיעא ולם ישגל באלה באחדהמא. פכאן מן לטף אלכ'אלק תעאלי באלאנסאן אן שגלה באמור דניאה ואכ'רתה לישתגל טול מדהֵ חיאתה פי ד'לך, פלא יטלב מא לא יעניה ולא ידרכה בעקלה, מת'ל אמור אלאבתדא ואלאנתהא, כקולה גם את העולם נתן בלבם מבלי אשר לא ימצא האדם את המעשה אשר עשה האלהים מראש ועד סוף. פאן כאן מות'רא לטאעהֵ אללה, מכ'תארא לעבאדתה, מתוכלא עליה פי אמור דינה ודניאה, מתנזהא ען אלרד'איל, מתשוקא אלי אלפצ'איל, לא תבטרה אלראחה ולא יאנס

The image of proximate causes, in the drawing forth of water from the depth of the earth by the wheel, is in the buckets that lift the water by the well-mechanism from the well. As for its remote cause, it is the human who yokes the beast to the well-mechanism, who moves it to lift the water from the bottom of the well to the surface of the earth. As for the causes between the human and the buckets, they are intermediaries between the two matters: the beast, the gears that turn one another, and the rope. If a defect befalls one of the mentioned causes, the intended purpose is not completed by them. So too the rest of the actions flowing into the bound of being: they are made valid by the human and another only by the decree of God (exalted be He) and His enabling them with the causes by which their completion comes — as He said: "For a God of knowledge is the Lord, and by Him deeds are weighed" (1 Samuel 2:3); and He said: "Great in counsel and abundant in deed" (Jeremiah 32:19); and He said: "For it was a turn of events from the Lord" (1 Kings 12:15). When the causes are wholly absent, the going-forth of the thing from the natural actions to the bound of being is not completed.

When we have considered the necessity of the human to the engagement and the causing for the completion of his matters, we find it going forth into plain sight: for the one who needs nourishment, when food has been set in front of him in what agrees with him — if he does not engage with eating it by lifting it to his mouth and chewing it — the gap of his hunger is not closed; and so the thirsty one in his need of water. How much, then, when food becomes impossible to him without his engaging with its preparation by grinding, kneading, cooking, and the like; and stronger and more emphatic is the engagement, if he needs to purchase it and prepare it; and yet more, if the price by which he buys it is impossible to him: he needs an engagement and a causing stronger than what was mentioned before — either he hires himself out for the price, or he sells what he cannot do without of furniture and goods and the like.

The reason on account of which God has bound the human to engagement with the causes of sustenance and of the rest of what he needs is twofold. The first: because wisdom required the testing of the soul in this world by obedience and disobedience; He has tried it with what makes that manifest from it — namely, neediness and want for what is outside it of food and drink and clothing and dwelling and marriage. He has commanded it to engage in attracting these by the causes prepared for it in specific aspects and at known times. What God has decreed to be completed for the human of these is completed and made valid by the soundness of the coming of the causes; what God has not decreed to be completed for him is not completed, and the causes become impossible for him; and obedience and disobedience to God (mighty and exalted) are validly attributed to him by intent and choice for one of them and not the other, and that necessitates reward and punishment, even if the carrying-out of the act has not been validly completed by the human.
